title: Workspace Heartbeat Executor Liveness v1
goal: Give the operator, inside the existing Heartbeat card and without opening a new chat, an independent view of demonstrated assistant-executor liveness that remains useful when the ChatGPT website says connection interrupted. Keep semantic progress and executor activity separate, then use the same observation layer later for bounded stale-owner recovery.
acceptance_criteria: The existing live Heartbeat card shows three independent concepts: Heartbeat/server connectivity, executor/model activity freshness, and last meaningful semantic progress.

Add a model-only heartbeat_touch(task_id, turn_id) operation that renews executor activity without creating a semantic Heartbeat entry, changing semantic sequence/history, or adding another transcript card.
heartbeat_begin_turn and heartbeat_update also count as executor touches.
The live card records UI observation separately when its app-only snapshot poll succeeds, so browser/card connectivity is distinguishable from executor activity.
Expose last_executor_touch_at and last_ui_seen_at plus their ages in the turn snapshot without exposing openai/session.

Display executor status as recent demonstrated activity, not as proof of internal process existence; stale means no recent executor signal, because ChatGPT exposes no documented assistant-turn terminal event to this MCP server.
Keep current semantic Heartbeat history, grow-through-five/scroll-from-six behavior, and turn isolation unchanged.
Do not require heartbeat_get or a second conversation to inspect executor freshness; the currently mounted live card must update itself.
Do not create a visible history entry or resize event merely because heartbeat_touch occurred.
Keep cross-conversation ownership fail-closed while a future lease is fresh; automatic takeover remains a later phase and is not required for the same-chat status MVP.
Before any takeover semantics are enabled, collect field evidence during a real frontend interruption and choose the lease TTL from measured touch gaps rather than guessing a fixed ChatGPT timeout.
constraints: Do not modify or deploy the live Heartbeat runtime until workspace-heartbeat-plugin-v1 v0.4.6 PR #155 completes its remaining host gates and is merged or otherwise durably accepted.
Do not claim exact internal ChatGPT executor death is observable unless OpenAI exposes a documented ChatGPT turn/session terminal signal to custom MCP servers.
Do not treat an individual Streamable HTTP request/socket close as assistant-turn death; the current server creates a request-scoped MCP transport.
Keep executor lease traffic separate from user-facing semantic heartbeat history and UI updates.
Use _meta["openai/session"] only as anonymized conversation ownership evidence; never expose or persist it in operator-visible output.
Do not weaken current cross-conversation ownership merely to recover faster; takeover requires an expired lease and must atomically fence the old turn.
Do not rely on a guessed 40-minute timeout. Current field evidence includes one Heartbeat turn with updates spanning about 47 minutes and another spanning about 37 minutes.
Do not claim the Heartbeat server can physically prevent direct mutations through unrelated tools; enforcement outside Heartbeat remains an executor/procedure contract unless a future proxy is added.
Persist design/acceptance evidence in workspace-control, but keep per-touch runtime lease state ephemeral.

evidence: User explicitly wants to know whether the current assistant response is still working from the existing broken/disconnected chat, without opening another chat.
Semantic Heartbeat timestamps are not liveness signals because updates are intentionally emitted only on meaningful semantic changes.
Current custom MCP server can observe model tool calls and app snapshot polls, but does not receive a documented whole-assistant-turn terminal event.
Request/HTTP connection close is request-scoped and cannot be treated as executor death.

notes:
Created from live field evidence on 2026-10-22/23. The user specifically observed the ChatGPT website disconnect while the server-side assistant continued to emit Heartbeat updates, followed later by Heartbeat silence. Current custom MCP tools do not receive a documented ChatGPT assistant-turn terminal event, so the design must distinguish exact internal death (currently unobservable) from operational liveness (measurable and recoverable). The proposed lease is intentionally machine-facing and must not reintroduce noisy timed semantic heartbeat updates.

2026-10-23 requirement refinement: the primary operator goal is same-chat observability, not recovery from a second conversation. The operator wants the already-mounted Heartbeat card to remain useful after the ChatGPT page reports connection interrupted and to show whether the assistant executor has recently demonstrated activity. Semantic Heartbeat updates must remain sparse and meaningful. The liveness MVP therefore adds a silent heartbeat_touch path and independent UI/executor timestamps; takeover is explicitly deferred until field measurement.

Node v20.20.2 npm test passed 27/27; isolated :8788 startup, pre-cutover v0.4.6 health, v0.4.6 rollback preservation, live :8787 health, verified v0.4.7 runtime CWD, and public ngrok health all PASS. ChatGPT plugin refresh exposed heartbeat_touch. Live same-card field observation then proved the three signals are independent in practice: the operator directly observed Executor freshness updating while Semantic progress did not change; after touch traffic stopped, the card continued polling while Executor and Semantic ages advanced. This is PASS for observation-only same-card signal separation. The remaining unproven field gate is persistence/usefulness across an actual ChatGPT frontend 'Connection interrupted' event; automatic takeover and TTL remain deferred.

2026-10-23 executor-touch policy integration: live field use exposed two false-stale executor indicators while substantive task work continued. Root cause was contractual: heartbeat_touch existed and the card consumed last_executor_touch_at, but procedures/progress_heartbeat.md had no deterministic emission rule. The live card classifies executor activity as recent only at <=30 seconds. The canonical policy now uses an operation-based backstop the model can actually obey: at most three non-Heartbeat tool operations between begin/update/touch signals during active execution, plus a touch before known long/opaque waits and during repeated polling. Touches remain silent and explicitly do not reset the independent 10-tool semantic-progress backstop.
